meta.title: Rivers of Punjab
meta.description: 10 handpicked MCQs on origins, dams, ancient names and key facts — with explanations and memory tricks to lock it in.
meta.author: Gurpreet Singh, Sub Inspector, Punjab Police

questions.q: During the Rigveda period, Punjab was known as the:
questions.trick: Rig = Rigveda = 7 (Sapta Sindhu era, more rivers incl. Saraswati)
questions.exp: In the Rigveda period Punjab was called the Land of Seven Rivers (Indus, Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum, Saraswati).

questions.q: The 'Land of Seven Rivers' included all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.trick: Yamuna belongs to the Gangetic system, not Punjab's rivers
questions.exp: The Seven Rivers were Indus, Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum and Saraswati. Yamuna was never part of this group.

questions.q: The word 'Punjab' is derived from which language, and what does it mean?
questions.pyq: One of the most repeated etymology questions
questions.trick: Punj (5) + Aab (Water) = Punjab, both Persian words
questions.exp: 'Punjab' comes from Persian: Punj (Five) + Aab (Water) = 'Land of Five Waters'.

questions.q: What was the Greek name for the Punjab region?
questions.exp: The Greeks called Punjab Pentopotamia, the Greek equivalent of 'Punjab'.

questions.q: Which river is the longest flowing in Punjab, and where does it originate?
questions.exp: The Sutlej is the longest river in Punjab, originating from Rakas Lake near Mansarovar and entering Punjab near Ropar.

questions.q: On which river is the Bhakra Nangal Dam built, and where does the river enter Punjab?
questions.pyq: Dam-river pairing is a classic exam favourite
questions.trick: Bhakra Nangal = Big dam = longest river = Sutlej
questions.exp: The Bhakra Nangal Dam is on the Sutlej, which enters Punjab near Ropar.

questions.q: The Beas river originates from Beas Kund near which pass, and which dam is built on it?
questions.exp: The Beas originates near Rohtang Pass; the Pong Dam is built on it, entering Punjab at Hoshiarpur.

questions.q: Which river is the SHORTEST flowing in Punjab, and on which river is the Ranjit Sagar Dam built?
questions.trick: Ravi = shortest river; enters at Pathankot
questions.exp: The Ravi is the shortest river in Punjab; the Ranjit Sagar Dam is built on it.

questions.q: The Ghaggar river is best described as a:
opts: Seasonal river that flows mainly in the rainy season
questions.pyq: Tests understanding of perennial vs seasonal rivers
questions.trick: Ghaggar 'disappears' in dry months — seasonal, monsoon-dependent
questions.exp: The Ghaggar is a seasonal river flowing mainly in the rainy season, believed to be a remnant of the ancient Saraswati river.

questions.q: 'Trimab' and 'Panjnad' refer to which river confluences?
opts: Trimab: Beas+Sutlej meeting; Panjnad: all five rivers meeting
Trimab: Ravi+Chenab+Jhelum meeting; Panjnad: where Trimab meets Sutlej
Trimab: Sutlej origin; Panjnad: Beas origin
Trimab: Ghaggar+Saraswati meeting; Panjnad: Ravi meeting Chenab
questions.trick: Tri = 3 rivers meet at Trimab; Panj = 5, Panjnad = Trimab + Sutlej
questions.exp: Trimab is where Ravi, Chenab and Jhelum meet. Panjnad is where the Trimab meets the Sutlej.
